grammar.label: the prepositional passive — this bed has been slept in
grammar.form: subject + be + past participle + stranded preposition
grammar.meaning: makes the object of a preposition the subject of the sentence

explanation.en: English can passivise across a preposition, which most languages cannot: 'Nobody has lived in the house' becomes 'The house has not been lived in.' The preposition stays behind, with nothing after it. This works only when the verb and preposition form a real unit — 'the bed was slept in' is fine, 'the room was slept in' is odd, because sleeping is not something you do to a room.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tili predlog orqali majhul nisbatga o'tishi mumkin: 'The house has not been lived in.' Predlog o'z joyida qoladi va undan keyin hech narsa kelmaydi. Bu ko'p tillarda mumkin emas.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek va rus tillarida predlogli majhul nisbat yo'q; bu tuzilma butunlay yangi va shuning uchun og'ir.

grammar.label: the double passive and the raising passive
grammar.form: is said / thought / believed / expected + to-infinitive; is expected to be completed
grammar.meaning: reports a general view without naming who holds it

explanation.en: 'The bridge is expected to be completed by June' has two passives: the expecting is attributed to nobody, and the completing is done by nobody. This is the workhorse of official English, and its danger is exactly its usefulness — it removes every agent, so nobody is responsible for either the expectation or the work.
explanation.uz: 'The bridge is expected to be completed by June' — ikkita majhul nisbat: kim kutmoqda va kim qurmoqda — ikkalasi ham ko'rsatilmagan. Rasmiy ingliz tilining asosiy quroli, xavfi ham shunda.

grammar.positive_example: The figures are understood to have been revised twice before publication.

story.title: The house has not been lived in

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The ministry's reply came this morning. Two pages and not one person named in it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The bridge is expected to be completed by June.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Expected by whom, and completed by whom?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Neither is in the sentence. There are two passives stacked on each other.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Every ministry in the world writes like that. It is not by itself a lie.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: It is when the whole letter is written in it.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then say that in your reply, and say it without doing the same thing yourself.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There is one I like. 'The clause was argued over for a fortnight and then left unchanged.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: A preposition passive, and the preposition has nothing after it.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Which would put the object back and break the sentence. English leaves the preposition at the end with nothing after it.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The house at the top of the lane has not been lived in since 2004.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Same shape, and nobody who says it thinks about it twice.
